demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Triggers.value: Physical pain in a part of the body

Threat.value: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
I watch other people closely for signs that they might harm me

Memory.value: When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief

Negative Appraisals.value: There is something about me that made the event happen
I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me

vignette:
Mark had always found solace in the quiet expanses of the woods, where the towering trees and rustling leaves offered him a sanctuary from the noise of the world. As a forester, he cherished his work, guiding others through nature's intricacies and nurturing the land he loved. Yet, everything changed on that fateful day a year ago when a simple miscalculation during a logging operation escalated into a catastrophic accident. In an instant, a branch he had intended to cut fell unexpectedly, striking a fellow worker, leaving him gravely injured. The moment played out like a haunting reel in Mark's mind, a scene that replayed with vivid clarity, each detail etched into his memory like a scar.

As weeks turned into months, Mark's life began to unravel. He found himself unable to shake off the physical pain that had settled into his body, an echo of the injury he had caused. Even in the most mundane of moments, he would feel a tightness in his chest, a sharpness in his shoulder, and he couldn't help but link it back to that day. Each ache reminded him of the harm he had inflicted, triggering memories of the victim's anguished face, and he often experienced a wave of guilt that left him breathless. It was not just the pain; it was the constant reminders that haunted him, creeping into his thoughts uninvited.

Mark's sense of safety eroded swiftly. No longer could he relax even in his own home, where the walls once provided comfort. He was hyper-vigilant, his heart racing at the slightest sound. When a stranger approached him at the local hardware store, he felt an overwhelming urge to retreat, convinced that even the most benign interactions could spiral into danger. He would watch other people closely, searching their expressions for signs of threat, a reflex now ingrained in his daily life. The forest, once a refuge, became a source of anxiety. The laughter of his colleagues during group outings felt like a reminder of the camaraderie he had lost and the fear that he might harm someone again.

The memories of that day would often wash over him like a tide, overwhelming him with grief and rage. He could vividly recall the sound of the branch snapping, the way time seemed to halt as he watched the accident unfold. Each recollection felt as though his body were reenacting that moment, a visceral connection that left him trembling and filled with remorse. He was no longer the confident forester who could navigate the woods with ease; instead, he felt like a ghost of his former self, haunted by the weight of his actions.

Mark had come to believe there was something intrinsically flawed about him, a deep-seated belief that he had brought this tragedy upon himself. This intrinsic fault suffocated him, leading to a pervasive sense of self-doubt. He struggled to trust his own judgment, convinced that he could no longer rely on himself in any capacity. The once vibrant man who had relished the outdoors now felt incapable of doing the very things that had defined him for most of his life. His wife, Sarah, noticed the changes too; their conversations had grown strained, filled with silences that felt heavier than words. Mark found himself withdrawing from her, unable to share the turmoil swirling inside him, fearing that his grief and guilt would push her away.

The culmination of his distress brought Mark to a tipping point. He realized he could no longer navigate this darkness alone. He needed help. The decision to seek therapy emerged not from a place of acceptance, but from a desperate hope to reclaim his life. Mark feared that he might never feel whole again, that the shadows of his past would always loom large. Yet, there was a flicker of hope within him-a hope that perhaps, with guidance, he could learn to forgive himself, to find a way back to the man he used to be, and maybe, just maybe, find peace in the woods once more.
